correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the 2x2 Hermitian concentration matrix with diagonal 2a/(2π), off-diagonal Z/(2π), and eigenvalue (2a+|Z|)/(2π). For the canonical phase arc, the missed and added densities both have mass m and are bounded by 1. Strict monotone cosine bathtub rearrangement gives exact inner/outer caps as the unique equality masks and yields |Z|≤2sin a(2cos(m/2)-1). Positivity of |Z| and 0≤m≤π force m<2π/3. Every feasible E_{a,m} is phase-aligned because its computed Z is strictly positive; all inequalities are then equalities. Symbolic trigonometric identities and finite-grid independent formula checks support, but do not replace, this proof.

originality.rationale: Source-scope and implication comparison: the primary 2026 circle theorem gives only the unrestricted interval maximum. The claim adds a pointwise sharp fixed-exchanged-mass nonlinear profile, an unconditional upper ceiling on phase-aligned defect, a soft-mask relaxation, and all equality masks. Four synonym/parameter queries returned no equivalent mathematical statement; the closest publicly indexed results concern discrete cyclic masks, unrelated moment norms, or real-line prolate detachment. Broader quantitative rearrangement theory is a residual risk but an unspecified nonsharp remainder does not entail the exact profile and equality classification. Claim correctness does not itself establish originality; this is a best-evidence originality assessment with openly specified access limits.
residual_risks: The full texts of Zelent (arXiv:2610.01299v1) and Cianchi–Ferone (2008) were not obtained, so their exact consequences cannot be exhaustively excluded.

No conclusion about degree two or higher follows from the elementary two-mode argument.

value.rationale: The first nonconstant Fourier concentration problem is the minimal natural spectral model of contemporary interval-optimality and stability questions. It obtains the globally sharp nonlinear stability function for every phase-centred exchanged mass, determines all extremizers even in the relaxed fractional-mask class, and discovers an intrinsic strict 2π/3 phase-compatibility restriction; this goes beyond a normalization or a tiny constant gain. The sharp parameterwise complete classification can calibrate future higher-degree concentration theory, without asserting broader theorems.
